subject: Linguistics
title: Language and Media
description: A quick win: understand Language and Media.

hook.text: 'Protesters' or 'rioters'? The word a news outlet chooses tells you its stance before the story starts.

buildup.text: Media language shapes public opinion through word choice, headlines, and narrative framing.

discovery.text: Active voice ('police shot protester') vs passive ('protester was shot') shifts blame and emphasis.

twist.text: Social media has democratized language—anyone can publish, but misinformation spreads alongside truth.

climax.text: Media literacy requires linguistic awareness—reading not just what's said, but how it's worded.

punchline.text: The news doesn't just report events—it frames them.

quiz.question: How does voice choice affect news reporting?
options: Active vs passive voice shifts blame and emphasis
